chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq, from Ali ibn Asbat, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

He said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, begins by looking at the visitors of the grave of Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) on the evening of Arafah. I said: Before He looks at the people of the Standing (at Arafah)? He said: Yes. I said: How is that? He said: Because among those (the people of Arafah) are children of fornication, and among these (the visitors of Husayn) there are no children of fornication.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْمَوْقِفِ: People of the Standing (pilgrims at Arafah)

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah look at the visitors of Imam Husayn before the pilgrims of Arafah?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this rare meaning (ma'ani) from Imam al-Sadiq, highlighting a unique divine preference for the Ziyarat of Imam Husayn over the standing at Arafah on the evening of the 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah. The Imam attributes this distinction to the lineage purity of the visitors, noting that the pilgrims at Arafah include 'children of fornication' (those from temporary or non-permanent unions), whereas the visitors of Husayn are free from this status. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual superiority of the Ahl al-Bayt's shrine and the specific merit of Ziyarat in the Shia tradition.

en.basel-kadem: 35.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal, from Ahmad bin Asheem, from al-Rida, peace be upon him, that he said:

I said to him: May I be sacrificed for you, why did the Arabs name their sons dog , tiger , leopard  and the likes of that? He said: The Arabs were people of war, and they used to frighten the enemy with the names of their children. Moreover, the used to name their slaves relief , blessed , fortunate  and the likes of that, by which they sought luck.
